html:
Same-sex marriage became legal in Taiwan on 24 May 2019, the first place in Asia to allow it.

The path ran through the courts. In May 2017 Taiwan's Constitutional Court ruled that limiting marriage to a man and a woman broke the constitution's promise of equality, and gave the legislature two years to act. In a referendum in November 2018 most voters said the civil code should not change. The legislature then passed a separate law in May 2019, just before the deadline.

Activists such as Chi Chia-wei had campaigned since the 1980s, when Taiwan was still under martial law. The change showed how far Taiwan's democracy had come since martial law ended in 1987. The Netherlands had been the first country to allow such marriages, in 2001. In Asia, Thailand followed in 2025.
sum: Same-sex marriage became legal in Taiwan on 24 May 2019, the first place in Asia to allow it.
